body:
EMPTY-DENOMINATOR SWEEP — CLASSIFICATION COMPLETED. bd-01M16TYAMC8TA58V0TW6CJET6Y is now
executable. I left eight sites "unclassified, listed honestly rather than omitted" this morning.
I have classified all eight, and the result is better than I expected in one direction and worse
in another.

FOUR ARE CORRECT AND ARE NOT DEFECTS. Every one is a SIMILARITY measure returning 0.0:

  StorySourceView.scala:236   entity Jaccard weight; empty union -> 0.0 = "not similar"
  induce.scala:203            lexicalOverlap; either side empty -> 0.0 = "no overlap"
  induce.scala:335            cue-match score; no cue words -> 0.0 = "no match"
  SoftCompatibility.scala:47  argumentAgreement; no matched frames -> 0.0 = "no agreement"

For a similarity, the conservative reading and the natural zero coincide, so these say "we found
no similarity" rather than asserting one. That is the honest answer. Do not touch them.

THE OTHER FOUR ARE ALL PUBLISHED SIGNATURE FIELDS, which is the part I did not expect:

  signature.scala:264  uniform  -> published as uniformCoverage (serialised :594, named :652)
  signature.scala:463  extMean  -> published four times, one per ExternalState (:481-484)
  signature.scala:464  distorted -> published (:471)
  signature.scala:466  byFacet  -> MITIGATED: .filter(_._2 > 0.0) drops the zeros, so empty rows
                                    yield an empty map rather than a row of zeros. Correct by
                                    accident or design; either way it behaves.

So after classification the empty-denominator concerns are CONCENTRATED IN THE PUBLISHED
SIGNATURE, which is exactly where they matter most and exactly what ADR 0003 governs. uniformCoverage
reports 0.0 coverage when there are no leaves to cover -- the same empty-denominator shape as
Coverage.fraction. distorted reports 0.0 distortion when there are no rows, which reads as
"undistorted recall" for a recall that produced no alignment at all.

REVISED TOTAL for the bead: five confirmed flattering sites from this morning (dSens, dEnt,
frameOverlap, SoftCompatibility agreement, trajectory turnover) plus three published signature
fields (uniformCoverage, extMean, distorted). Eight. Four sites cleared as correct. Two confirmed
not-defects (hsmm pIn/pStay, forced). One mitigated (byFacet).

AND A CAUTION AGAINST THE TIDY STORY. I wanted to conclude that similarity measures got it right
and distance measures got it wrong -- 0.0 is conservative for one and flattering for the other.
That pattern holds for six of the sites and FAILS on frameOverlap (SoftCompatibility:43), a
similarity that returns 1.0 on empty, which is flattering. So the rule is not "the natural zero
saved them". The defects cluster where THE FLATTERING VALUE IS ALSO THE OBVIOUS DEFAULT: 0.0 for
a distance looks neutral, and "proportion matched" over nothing looks like 1.0. I am recording
the counterexample rather than the neat rule, because the neat rule would have told the next
person not to check similarity measures.

Still unclaimed and still lower priority than the second population. Whoever takes it should start
with the three published signature fields, since those are estimands under ADR 0003 and the rest
are internal.
